questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “RTOS and FreeRTOS foundations”?
options: `vTaskDelayUntil` preserves the intended period, but long blocking work can still miss a deadline.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
An infinite task should block or wait periodically so it does not monopolize the CPU.
questions.answer: The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
questions.explanation:
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
Why: A real-time operating system (RTOS) divides work into tasks and schedules CPU time between them. It does not automatically make work faster; it makes timing and coordination explicit. ESP32 Arduino Core already runs FreeRTOS, so a sketch can create tasks. For a single LED or sensor, ordinary `loop()` is often simpler.
